tob-10469: Part I-II of Aquinas’s Summa Theologica turns from God to human life, asking what happiness is and how we reach it. Here he sets out his famous account of the virtues, the vices, and the law — the moral architecture that underlies Catholic ethics to this day. Readers meet one of the most systematic minds in history working at full power.
tob-10969: The complete Douay-Rheims Bible gave English-speaking Catholics their own translation of the Scriptures, rendered from the Latin Vulgate by scholars of the English College at Douai. Its Old Testament appeared in 1609–10 and its New Testament in 1582, later polished by Bishop Challoner. For centuries this was the Bible of the English Catholic household.
tob-0169: The Eddas are the well of Norse myth — the songs of Odin, Thor, and Loki, the shaping of the world, and its fiery end at Ragnarök. This volume joins the Elder (poetic) Edda to Snorri Sturluson’s prose retelling. Together they keep the tales that molded Viking belief and still feed today’s fantasy.
cia-0000106269: A November 1964 situation report filed at 8:30 in the evening local time, on rising tension in Vientiane between Laos's national police and rival factions. Laos was a three-way battleground of neutralists, rightists, and communists, and the capital could tip toward street fighting at any moment. The timestamped format shows intelligence reporting as it happened.
cia-0000109069: A September 1967 report on Cuban leaders criticizing Soviet foreign and domestic policies. Havana's public scolding of its patron revealed real strain — Castro resented playing junior partner. The document shows the CIA collecting every sign of friction, hoping the communist alliance might crack.
cia-0000119169: A February 1961 forecast of prospects for British Guiana — the colony heading toward independence as Guyana. Washington already worried about its Marxist-leaning leader, Cheddi Jagan. The document shows the CIA gaming out a small colony's future two years before the crisis peaked.
cia-0000124269: A November 1957 report on Czechoslovakia's alleged contribution to the Sputnik launch. The satellite that shocked the world in October 1957 was a Soviet triumph — but who else helped? The document shows the CIA picking apart the great Soviet achievement for its hidden contributors.
cia-0000119769: An August 1956 report on Hungarian writers demanding freedom of expression. The Petofi Circle debates — intellectuals challenging censorship — were the revolution's literary prelude. The document shows the uprising beginning with words, months before it continued with stones and guns.
cia-0000126869: An October 1979 Near East and South Asia review on the outlook for the Afghan insurgency — the truncated title cuts off the timeframe. Two months before the Soviet invasion, the rebels were already gaining. The document is the calm before the superpower blunder: Afghanistan, about to swallow an empire.
cia-0000132169: Situation Report 487 on political developments, including Iraqi terrorist killings — the truncated title cuts off the details. As the air war pounded Iraq, Baghdad lashed out through terror. The document records the war's shadow campaign alongside its politics.
cia-0000132569: An October 1960 report on East Germany and Cuba establishing closer cultural ties. The bloc's members courted Havana each in their own way — even with concerts and exchanges. The document is the soft side of the alliance: the culture, exchanged.
cia-0000132669: A 1961 report: Latin American reactions to the Cuban situation. The continent kept rendering its verdict. The document is the chorus: the reactions, gathered.
cia-0000132769: A 1960 Cuban situation report: economic agreements with the bloc, a Latin American youth congress — the truncated title hints at more. Deals and gatherings. The document is the week: the agreements, the congress, the island.
cia-0000134269: Item 16 in a 1960 Latin America series: communists extending Cuba-based activities across Latin America — the truncated title cuts off the region. Havana was the hub; the continent, the target. The document is the network: the activities, spreading.
cia-0000135869: A 1952 report on the current planning of the Calligeris organization, with attachments. Calligeris was a cryptonym — the exile network, organizing. The entry is the plan: the organization, plotting.
cia-0000135969: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting the scanning of students' personnel records. The operation was vetting recruits — or hunting infiltrators. The document is the screen: the records, scanned.
cia-0000136069: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on preventing red penetration. The operation guarded against communist infiltration. The document is the defense: the penetration, prevented.
cia-0000136169: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for PAGE on WSBURNT military matters. The target country's forces, discussed. The document is the brief: the military, covered.
cia-0000136269: The daily situation report number 06, 1954. The sixth day. The document is the routine: the day, numbered.
cia-0000136369: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting SKIMMER contact with Calligeris soonest — the archive's spelling doubles the l, the truncated title cuts off the purpose. The urgent meeting. The entry is the request: the contact, soonest.
cia-0000136969: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN suggesting BRODFROST advise STORAX of plane flights — the truncated title cuts off the details. The coordination, suggested. The document is the advice: the flights, notified.
cia-0000137469: 1961 situation reports on Venezuela. The year's file. The document is the series: the republic, reported.
cia-0000139169: A 1978 file of excerpts from a daily dairy — the typo repeats. The days, sampled. The document is the excerpt: the diary, distilled.
cia-0000139369: NIE 11-4-61: the main trends in Soviet capabilities and policies, 1961 to 1965 — the archive's spelling says trands — with an annex, the truncated title suggests. The five-year forecast. The document is the estimate: the trends, projected — through a typo.
un-ga-res-a-69-69: Resolution A/69/69, cataloged with the year 1961 — the session-year mismatch appears again. The designation is preserved; the date is doubted. The entry is honest about the riddle.
un-sc-res-369: Security Council Resolution 369, adopted in 1975. The Council's business rolled on. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-969: Security Council Resolution 969, adopted in 1995 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1269: Security Council Resolution 1269, adopted in October 1999 — the terrorism cooperation resolution, calling on all states to deny safe haven and cooperate against international terrorism. Two years before September 11, the Council named the coming war. The resolution is the call: the cooperation, demanded.
cia-0000136769: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136769, the archive's date uncertain, closing the 2506 run. The circa papers. The entry is the close: the run, complete — the dating, soft.
un-ga-res-34-169: General Assembly Resolution 34/169, cataloged with the year 1966 — the historical record places this Code of Conduct for Law Enforcement Officials in December 1979, setting global standards for police behavior. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d69: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 29, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 69. A second letter the same day. The message is the doubling: the day, busy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d169: The President to the Secretary of State, October 26, 1943 — Document 169. A second that day. The message is the doubling: the day, busy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d269: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 25, 1943 — Document 269. Thanksgiving Day, the planners met. The minutes are the holiday session: the chiefs, working.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d369: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 30, 1943 — Document 369. The month's last planners' session. The minutes are the month's end: the chiefs, closing November.
jim-davis-pg7369: John Masefield's Jim Davis — smugglers, Devon coasts, and boyish daring — thrilled young readers. The future Poet Laureate's adventure classic. Salt spray and excitement on every page. Moonlit coves and revenue cutters frame his smuggling tale. Masefield's tale remains a boy's book classic.
arxiv-2605-08769: When several AI agents tackle a job together, someone must decide who does what and in which order. A team at Sun Yat-Sen University led by Chengdong Xu and Kaiqiang Ke presents EvoMAS, a method that learns those execution-time workflows while the agents are actually running instead of following a fixed script. The paper describes how the learned plans adapt as multi-agent tasks unfold.
arxiv-2605-08869: Which corners of AI are growing fastest, and which are quietly shrinking? Zeyu Li, Yalan Jin, Shuyu Chen, Tingxin Jiang, and Xinyi Chang answer with bibliometrics — counting publications across AI subfields, comparing them side by side and tracking them over time. The 2026 paper is a data-driven map of where the field is actually heading.
arxiv-2605-09069: Hyperbolic equations model waves; when they degenerate inside the domain, standard approximations stumble. Dong-Hui Yang and Bao-Zhu Guo approximate such degenerate equations with interior degeneracy, with applications to controllability — steering the system where you want it. The 2026 paper is PDE analysis for difficult wave problems.
arxiv-2605-09169: Prediction bottlenecks — compressing data to predict well — were hoped to reveal causal structure for free. Ankit Hemant Lade, Sai Krishna Jasti, Indar Kumar, and colleagues show they do not, then explain what the bottlenecks actually do. The 2026 paper is a myth-busting study in causal representation learning.
arxiv-2605-09569: Finding a hidden submatrix — a needle of signal in a haystack of noise — has fundamental statistical limits. Parker Knight and Julien Chhor pin down minimax-optimal detection with sharp non-asymptotic rates. The 2026 paper is high-dimensional statistics at its sharpest.
arxiv-2605-09769: Psychological defense mechanisms — denial, projection, rationalization — hide in text, and classifying them is subtle work. Dima Galat and Marian-Andrei Rizoiu pit multi-agent councils against the task, reasoning from absence as well as presence. The 2026 paper is NLP for the human psyche.
arxiv-2605-09969: The truth lies somewhere in the middle — of the generated tokens. Sophie L. Wang, Phillip Isola, and Brian Cheung locate precisely where in a generation the truth hides. The 2026 paper is about positional honesty in language models. It maps honesty across token positions.
arxiv-2605-10069: Epidemic trajectories need consensus estimates — via a constrained power Fréchet mean with functional registration. Yui Tomo, Shu Tamano, and Daisuke Yoneoka develop the estimator. The 2026 paper is epidemic statistics with geometric averaging. It finds the consensus epidemic curve.
plos-pone-0003369: Molecular biologists mapped the cargo of a busy protein in this 2008 genetics paper. SF2/ASF, a well-known regulator of how gene instructions get spliced, also shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm carrying mRNA targets. The researchers identified which messages it handles in each compartment, clarifying its roles in splicing, export, and building proteins.
plos-pone-0003469: Cancer researchers hunted tumor stem cells in bone cancer in this 2008 paper. Osteosarcoma, the most common primary bone tumor, contains mixed cell populations, and the team isolated the CD133-marked cells suspected of driving regrowth. Characterizing these cancer stem cells in solid tumors points to the root that therapies must kill to prevent relapse.
plos-pone-0003569: Evolutionary geneticists Cai and Clapham traced a fast-changing fertility channel in this 2008 paper. The CatSper family of sperm-specific calcium channels, essential for the hyperactive swimming that reaches the egg, showed lineage-specific gene loss and rapid evolution across mammals. The restless history points to sperm competition as a driver of reproductive innovation.
plos-pone-0003669: In 2008, a team hunted new drug targets for Rett syndrome in mice. Girls with Rett, a disorder tied to the MECP2 gene, lose skills after early normal growth, and mice missing Mecp2 model the disease. The team mapped fresh neuronal targets in these mice, opening new routes toward treating a severe childhood disorder.
plos-pone-0003769: Wang, Wang, and Li found a notorious gene guarding brain-tumor roots in this 2008 paper. The c-Myc oncogene proved required to maintain glioma cancer stem cells, the self-renewing core of lethal brain tumors. Knocking out Myc's support collapses the hierarchy that makes gliomas so hard to kill.
plos-pone-0003869: In 2008, Jain, Dey, and Dhar built a better TB vaccine candidate. Their recombinant BCG carrying Ag85C gave stronger, longer-lasting protection against tuberculosis in tests. The improved shot addresses BCG's famously patchy record against adult TB.
plos-pone-0003969: In 2008, Horne, Phillips, and Kane linked a cannabis receptor to ectopic pregnancy. Women with tubal pregnancies showed lower CB1 levels in fallopian tube and decidua tissue. Without normal CB1 signaling, embryos may stall in the tube instead of reaching the womb. The finding points to the endocannabinoid system as a player in healthy implantation.
plos-pone-0004069: In 2008, Fischer, Nagel, and Jacobs re-mapped a key cancer-homing receptor. Their new antibody reassessed CXCR4 expression across normal and tumor tissues. The chemokine receptor guides cancer cells to spread sites. The cleaner map sharpens its value as a drug target.
plos-pone-0004169: In 2009, Heidelberg, Nelson, and Schoenfeld read germ warfare in a microbial mat. CRISPR arrays recorded the co-evolution of hosts and their viruses. The natural archive showed viral immunity evolving in the wild. The ancient ledger informs modern CRISPR use today.
plos-pone-0004269: In 2009, Reeves and Richards sharpened the genetic mapmaker's lens. Principal coordinates analysis inferred subtle population structure. The method caught fine genetic breaks other tools missed. The approach aids biodiversity and breeding studies. The math turns raw markers into clear population maps.
plos-pone-0004369: In 2009, Castle, Hara, and Raymond found a fat enzyme's hidden face. ACC2 ran high in human white adipose tissue with a novel N-terminal isoform. The metabolic enzyme's new form was mapped fully. The finding spotlights an obesity drug target today.
plos-pone-0359069: Myasthenia gravis is a disease that leaves muscles weak and easily tired. This genetics study identifies a single-letter change in DNA, rs28362336, linked to a higher risk of the generalized form of the disease. The authors also examine how this variant affects a nearby gene, HCG27, offering a new clue about why some people develop the condition and where future treatments might aim.
plos-pone-0357469: A newborn’s gut bacteria mostly come from its parents — and this study shows the effect runs deeper than digestion. In newborn mice, the parental intestinal microbiome shaped levels of glucocorticoids, the stress hormones, both throughout the body and in local tissues. The finding hints that a parent’s gut health could influence how a newborn handles stress.
plos-pone-0358769: When hackers or disasters knock out part of a network, the damage spreads from where the attack starts. This paper studies how the position of the initial ‘seed’ node shapes a network’s survival under localized attacks. The findings point to which spots in a network are the most dangerous points of failure.
plos-pone-0355369: Online COVID communities formed and fractured at astonishing speed. This paper maps the rapid organization of these groups, treating their shifts like tectonic plates grinding and splitting. The analysis shows how crisis forges and breaks digital communities — lessons for managing the next pandemic’s information chaos.
plos-pone-0358969: 3D-printed honeycomb panels could make things strong and light — if the print settings are right. This study experimentally tested FFF-printed PLA honeycomb sandwich panels for bending strength and mass efficiency, optimizing across multiple responses. The design rules help engineers print panels that carry more with less.
plos-pone-0356869: Aging well may start with how kindly you treat yourself. This study linked self-compassion and self-efficacy to pain, health behaviors, postural awareness, and quality of life in healthy aging. The associations suggest inner resources matter as much as outer ones for growing old in good shape.
plos-pone-0350969: Growing vegetables against the season can lift Cambodian farmers’ incomes — if the gamble pays. This paper studied the impact of off-season vegetable production in Cambodia. The results show whether bucking the calendar pays off, which farmers benefit most, and what risks they carry.
plos-pone-0358469: Cattle farms can store carbon in their soils — depending on how the land is used. This paper measured soil organic carbon stocks, litter decomposition, and soil macrofauna diversity across contrasting land uses on a dual-purpose cattle farm in Colombia. The comparison shows which practices keep carbon in the ground and which let it escape.
plos-pone-0358069: Therapeutic plasma exchange — filtering harmful substances from the blood — treats a surprising range of diseases. This seven-year real-world cohort from an Egyptian tertiary center studied its use across multiple organ systems. The long record shows what the therapy genuinely achieves outside the controlled world of trials.
plos-pone-0358269: Loneliness in Japan shifted dramatically through the pandemic years. This longitudinal study explored transitions in loneliness across 2020–2024, tracking who moved in and out of isolation. The trajectories reveal who recovered socially as restrictions lifted — and who remained stuck alone.
plos-pone-0356569: Caring for a loved one with an enterostomy — a surgically created abdominal opening — is demanding, skilled work. This evidence summary distilled optimization strategies for family caregivers’ care-giving behaviors. The strategies help families provide safer, more confident stoma care at home.
plos-pone-0356769: When a transplanted kidney fails in the UK, what happens next isn’t equal for everyone. This paper documented inequalities in outcomes after kidney transplant failure. The disparities — by ethnicity, deprivation, and more — demand that transplant programs confront their own inequities.
plos-pone-0353069: Dengue forecasting needs different tools for next week versus next season. This paper proposed an adaptable framework for horizon-dependent dengue forecasting using data-driven approaches with serotype and climate covariates in Bangladesh. The flexible framework matches the forecast method to the decision at hand.
plos-pone-0356269: The chemistry of a dead heart can reveal how it died. This paper applied targeted metabolomics — using the Biocrates MxP Quant 500 kit — to postmortem human cardiac tissue. The metabolic fingerprints offer forensic pathologists molecular clues about cardiac death that autopsy alone cannot provide.
plos-pone-0356469: Tribal communities in hard-to-reach areas need TB knowledge that sticks. This paper reported tuberculosis knowledge, attitude, and practice findings among volunteers after community-based intervention training. The outcome evaluation shows whether training tribal volunteers genuinely moves the needle on TB awareness.
plos-pone-0355969: Grading cataracts by AI could bring eye screening to places without specialists. This feasibility study tested artificial intelligence-based grading of human cataracts. The promising results suggest automated grading could triage the millions awaiting cataract surgery worldwide.
plos-pone-0353169: Fona herzogae — a small herbivorous dinosaur from Utah’s Cretaceous — gets its skull described in detail. This paper presented the cranial osteology of the thescelosaurine from the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation. The anatomical description illuminates the life of a burrowing dinosaur.
plos-pone-0352669: Pyruvate kinase activators — potential drugs for blood disorders — can be found by computer. This paper used integrative molecular simulations to identify candidates, moving from structural insight to molecule. The computational pipeline accelerates drug discovery for diseases of red cell metabolism.
plos-pone-0354669: Predicting which drugs will kill which cancers could personalize oncology. This paper predicted drug sensitivity across cancer types using graph isomorphism networks with biological pathway features in a dual-branch deep learning approach. The pathway-aware AI matches tumors to their most vulnerable drug targets.
plos-pone-0355869: Nasal swab types matter for respiratory virus detection. This Hawaiian study compared diagnostic agreement between Rhinoswabs and combined nose-and-throat swabs for influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in symptomatic outpatients. The comparison guides clinics toward the swab strategy that catches the most infections with least discomfort.
plos-pone-0355469: Sepsis kills through dysregulated immunity — and cell cycle genes may mark the chaos. This paper integrated bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to investigate cell cycle-related biomarkers in sepsis. The multi-scale analysis pinpoints molecular signals that could guide sepsis treatment.
europmc-pmc2838869: Gene-reading tech was fresh in 2010, with no pact on data cleanup. This paper pits data fixes against each other, testing scaling tricks and change-finding in mRNA-Seq runs. The authors crown sound habits. Their test steered a wave of gene readers to firm ground.
europmc-pmc2991069: The immune system reads a yeast's shape before answering. This 2010 paper shows skin cells give a two-phase alarm that tells round yeast from thread-like Candida. The authors reveal the shape-sensing trick. Their work clarifies fungal immunity. The second phase decides war or peace.
europmc-pmc3076369: River health got DNA barcoded. This 2011 paper IDs riverbed bugs by DNA to gauge water health. The authors' method speeds surveys hugely. Their work aids conservation. One sample replaces weeks of sorting. Regulators adopted it for river report cards. The method now spans continents.
europmc-pmc6536969: Traditional Chinese medicine has treated ailments for millennia, and modern labs are now testing its herbs against cancer. This review summarizes what science knows about TCM's anti-tumor effects: which compounds show activity, how they interfere with cancer cells, and where the evidence stands. The authors argue ancient remedies deserve rigorous modern trials, not dismissal.
europmc-pmc6538669: To copy itself, the SARS coronavirus builds an RNA-synthesizing machine centered on the nsp12 polymerase, aided by nsp7 and nsp8 cofactors. This study revealed the machine's three-dimensional structure - the first atomic-level look at a coronavirus replication engine. The blueprint showed drug designers exactly where to aim antivirals that jam viral copying.
europmc-pmc6582769: Brain scans reveal the mind as a network - regions linked like airports by flight routes. This systematic review shows how graph theory, the math of networks, maps those connections and spots the hubs and shortcuts behind thinking and disease. The approach turns tangled wiring diagrams into measurable patterns of human cognition.
europmc-pmc6756069: Humans suppress telomerase to keep cancer at bay - but tumors switch it back on. This review details how cancers reactivate TERT, the telomerase gene, through mutations and other tricks old and new. The activation playbook reveals targets for drugs that could re-silence the enzyme.
europmc-pmc6774269: Knowing which microbes are present is just the start - what are they doing? Metatranscriptomics reads the RNA microbes are actually expressing, and this review maps the field's advances and challenges. The activity readout moves microbiome science from census to biography.
gao-gaoreports-b-309869: KIC Development cried foul on a 2007 federal award, and GAO's ruling is the final word. The firm said the bid contest was run unfairly; the call tests each charge and rules. For companies in the government market, published calls like this double as case law — the fine print of fair play, written one dispute at a time.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-769: The SBA's flagship loan program was flying without gauges in 2007 — GAO's report says the 7(a) program needed real measures of success. The findings ask the basic question: did the guaranteed loans create lasting businesses? The report demands proof, not just activity.
gao-gaoreports-b-308969: Parking money in open-ended deals drew GAO's fiscal eye in 2007 — could funds be obligated this way under the interagency pact? The ruling reads the purse law against the contract vehicle. The call decides where the budget lines really sit.
gao-gaoreports-b-299369: AMS Group took its April 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call. The firm challenged the award as unfair; the ruling tests the claims in full. Short names get the same long, careful hearing in the protest process as the big players.
gao-gaoreports-b-299469: Knight's Armament Company took its April 2007 weapons-contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call. The arms maker challenged the award; the ruling tests the claims in full. Even gun deals go through the same bid-law mill as everything else.
openalex-w7207549069: A school's walls, wiring, and plumbing shape what happens inside its classrooms. This article surveys the physical state of rural and urban schools offering the final years of elementary education in Bahia's Piemonte Norte do Itapicuru region. It documents gaps between what the law promises for the right to education and what the buildings actually provide. The result is a detailed portrait of unequal conditions across one territory.
openalex-w7206168469: Cattle sometimes eat things they should not, soil, bones, plastic, a condition called depraved appetite or pica. This veterinary paper reviews the causes, signs, and consequences of feeding disorders in cattle, aiming to help ranchers prevent and manage them. It gathers what is known about triggers and herd-level impacts. Practical and farm-focused, it treats animal nutrition as both a welfare and an economic issue.
openalex-w7206170569: Hidradenitis suppurativa, also called acne inversa, is a painful chronic skin disease marked by recurring lumps, abscesses, and tunnels under the skin. It affects roughly one percent of the population and can be deeply debilitating. This narrative review pulls together current knowledge on how doctors diagnose it and what treatments help. Written for clinicians and patients alike, it offers a clear update on managing a condition that is often misunderstood.
openalex-w7205015369: Microgreens are tiny young vegetable and herb plants, and they pack a lot of nutrition into a few inches. This review covers how they are grown: their health perks, farm methods, useful traits, and market trends. Drawing on Brazilian and world research, the authors map a crop that rose from restaurant garnish to serious farming. Handy for growers eyeing a high-value niche and eaters curious about the hype.
openalex-w7204234769: Brazil's 2021 bidding law moved government buying onto online platforms. This study checks whether e-procurement made public buying cleaner and quicker. The authors test if the reform cut waste and sped up deals paid with public money. A nuts-and-bolts look at whether digital rules made the state's shopping better.
openalex-w4409743169: Stretch a soft crystal and its electrons switch sides. This lab paper measured electric resistance in an organic conductor while pulling and squeezing it, tracking its flip between metal and insulator. The team built a press to do it. A study of wringing new behavior from bendy crystals.
pmc-13471269: This 2026 medical study follows a population-based group of patients over time to ask whether men and women differ in their risk of dying after an aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage — bleeding from a burst brain aneurysm. Prospective, population-level data like this gives one of the most trustworthy answers to questions of sex difference in stroke outcomes.
pmc-13465769: A 2026 environmental biology paper on a three-way team — fungus, algae, and bacteria living with Euglena mutabilis — that tolerates cadmium, a toxic heavy metal. Combining gene-activity and hormone measurements, the authors mapped how the consortium survives the poison. Such consortia could one day clean up contaminated water.
pmc-13531469: This 2026 multicenter study reports long-term real-world treatment of cardiac transthyretin amyloidosis — a heart-stiffening protein-misfolding disease — with tafamidis. Real-world data over years complements the original trials. The findings confirm how the drug performs outside controlled settings.
pmc-13418369: In this 2026 study, researchers built an XGBoost machine-learning model — interpreted with Shapley values — to predict mild cognitive impairment in older Chinese patients with cerebral small vessel disease. Small vessel disease is a major cause of vascular dementia. The model turns routine clinical data into an early warning.
pmc-13544969: This 2026 bioinformatics paper introduces Theseus, a tool for fast and optimal affine-gap sequence-to-graph alignment. Aligning DNA reads to graph genomes — which capture population variation — is computationally demanding. Theseus makes it both faster and provably optimal.
pmc-13505169: This 2026 randomized controlled trial found eight weeks of focal muscle vibration improved muscle coordination and co-contraction in children with cerebral palsy. The simple intervention showed measurable benefit. The trial supports its use in rehab.
pmc-13489569: This 2026 trial studied protective effects of L-carnitine plus interval training on kidney and liver function in overweight and obese individuals. The supplement-exercise combo showed organ benefits. The trial supports the combined intervention.
pmc-13466369: This 2026 review examined estrogen receptors and estrogen-synthesis enzymes as breast cancer treatment targets. The hormone pathway remains druggable. The review organizes the target landscape.
pmc-13421569: This 2026 South African study captured experiences of home-based caregivers of chronic mental illness patients in Limpopo Province. The caregivers' voices are rarely heard. The study amplifies them.
pmc-13585469: In this 2026 software paper, SNIRF2BIDS — a GUI tool — converted fNIRS data to the Brain Imaging Data Structure in R. The converter eases data sharing. The tool is the deliverable.
pmc-13530469: This 2026 conference paper reviewed social media claims about "peptides" for musculoskeletal health — alleged indications, risks, and usage. The hype needed scrutiny. The paper provides it.
pmc-13529069: This 2026 prospective observational study examined the impact of concomitant meniscus repair with ACL reconstruction on short-term functional outcomes. Fixing both injuries together was evaluated. The outcomes guide surgical planning.
pmc-13500869: A 2026 paper on deep learning-based inclusion boundary identification using wave propagation in optical coherence elastography. The AI found tissue boundaries. The wave physics guided the learning.
pmc-13502869: In this 2026 study, low handgrip strength was associated with impaired gait and dexterity in degenerative cervical myelopathy patients. The hand's weakness signaled broader decline. The association is the clinical clue.
pmc-13492269: In this 2026 soil science paper, a diffusion-driven methane-oxygen boundary structured methane oxidation and carbon transformation in upland soils. The gas boundary organized the microbiology. The structuring is the mechanism.
pmc-13492469: A 2026 X-ray paper with sub-20 nm spectromicroscopy revealing nanoscale redox heterogeneity in ultrafine particulates. The air pollution particles' chemistry varied at the nanoscale. The heterogeneity is the finding.
pmc-13478369: A 2026 dosimetric study of photon energy and flattening filter mode combinations in stereotactic central ablative radiotherapy. The radiation physics was optimized. The study guides treatment planning.
pmc-13467169: A 2026 comprehensive review of developmental challenges and innovations in overcoming barriers in porcine somatic cell nuclear transfer. The cloning bottlenecks were surveyed. The review guides the field.
pmc-13463569: This 2026 paper offered insights into genetic diversity within the Auliekol cattle breed using SNP genotyping. The Kazakh breed's diversity was mapped. The genotyping is the resource.
pmc-13492369: In this 2026 computational chemistry paper, ligand binding modes were predicted by scaffold-guided structure refinement. The docking was guided by scaffolds. The refinement is the method.
pmc-13495369: In this 2026 AML paper, peritransplant molecular MRD monitoring by targeted NGS was performed in FLT3-ITD-mutated acute myeloid leukemia patients. The residual disease was tracked. The monitoring guides transplant decisions.
pmc-13594669: A 2026 analysis of UACR and UPCR association with kidney failure in patients with rare kidney diseases — using observational data. The urine markers predicted failure. The analysis guides monitoring.
pmc-13525169: A 2026 case report on using non-medical-grade ethyl cyanoacrylate (superglue) for temporary skin closure in a bleeding upper eyelid arteriovenous malformation. The improvised glue held. The case is the resourceful lesson.
pmc-13519269: This 2026 Nepalese study examined human risk factors associated with antibodies against Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex in captive Asian elephants from Chitwan valley (the title is truncated). The elephants' TB exposure was surveyed. The risk factors inform conservation.
pmc-13517569: A 2026 veterinary paper on poxvirus infections in common swifts. The aerial birds' viral disease was documented. The infections are the wildlife health data.
pmc-13473169: A 2026 study: neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio was associated with low muscle mass risk in rheumatoid arthritis — evidence from a hospital cohort and NHANES (the title is truncated). The inflammatory-nutritional ratio predicted sarcopenia. The association is the clinical signal.
pmc-13427669: A 2026 obstetrics paper revisiting the evidence for vaginal progesterone in short cervix — screening strategy versus drug efficacy. The prevention debate was reframed. The revisiting is the analysis.
pmc-13534469: This 2026 liver cancer paper used integrated single-cell multi-omics to reveal lipid-associated macrophage-mediated immunosuppression in neoadjuvant immunotherapy of hepatocellular carcinoma (the title is truncated).
